children: Accel and 360 ONE offload 61.98 lakh BlueStone shares for Rs 513 crore as mutual funds and insurers acquire stakes in the jewellery retailer
Institutional investors Accel and 360 ONE have offloaded a combined 61.98 lakh shares of omnichannel jewellery retailer BlueStone through multiple bulk and block deals, as per a media report

Accel India III Mauritius sold 28 lakh shares for Rs 231.7 crore, while four funds managed by 360 ONE sold nearly 34 lakh shares for Rs 281.3 crore. Each transaction was executed at Rs 827.60 per share, representing a 3 per cent premium to the stock's closing price
The shares were acquired by domestic mutual funds and insurance companies, along with some international investors
Mirae Asset Mutual Fund was the largest buyer, acquiring 20.8 lakh shares. Bajaj Life Insurance, SBI Life Insurance and Nippon India Mutual Fund each bought 9.5 lakh shares
Kuwait Investment Authority, Goldman Sachs and Citigroup Global Markets Singapore also acquired shares in the company
Overall, nearly 4 per cent of BlueStone's equity changed hands in the transactions, with the combined deal value standing at around Rs 513 crore

Accel held 1.6 crore BlueStone shares, or around 10.1 per cent of the company, as of June 30, 2026. The latest transaction represents 17.4 per cent of its holding. 360 ONE held around 3.8 per cent of BlueStone at the end of the June quarter

This is the second stake sale by the investors in BlueStone this year. In June, Accel, 360 ONE and IvyCap Ventures sold 46.4 lakh shares of the jewellery company through multiple open-market transactions for Rs 242.8 crore

Founded in 2011 by Gaurav Singh Kushwaha and Vidya Nataraj, BlueStone offers more than 8,000 designs across rings, pendants, earrings and other jewellery categories. The company competes with CaratLane, GIVA and other jewellery brands
BlueStone operated 352 stores across 139 cities as of the end of the June quarter, according to its disclosures
The company reported a profit after tax of Rs 6 crore in Q1 FY27, compared with a loss of Rs 34.8 crore in the year-ago period. However, profit declined 81 per cent sequentially
Operating revenue rose 50 per cent year-on-year and 8 per cent quarter-on-quarter to Rs 736.9 crore during the quarter
BlueStone shares ended the day's trading session 5.63 per cent lower at Rs 805.06
